questions.q: What does the IMU mainly measure?
questions.correct: The robot's heading, which way it is pointing
wrong: The robot's speed across the field floor
The battery's remaining charge level
The distance to the nearest field wall
questions.explain: The IMU has a gyroscope; its main output is heading — the robot's compass direction. You use it to know which way the robot faces.

questions.q: When the robot spins counter-clockwise, heading...
wrong: Drops toward −π
Stays exactly at 0
Jumps straight to 360
questions.explain: Heading starts at 0; spin left (counter-clockwise) and it grows toward +π, spin right and it drops toward −π. It's measured in radians.

questions.q: What units does FTC code read the IMU heading in?
wrong: Degrees
Inches
Percent
questions.explain: The code reads heading in radians because Math.cos and Math.sin expect radians. You convert to degrees only for human-readable telemetry.

wrong: imu.getHeadingInches()
imu.readCompass(DEGREES)
imu.getSpeed(RADIANS)
questions.explain: getRobotYawPitchRollAngles().getYaw(AngleUnit.RADIANS) returns the yaw (heading) in radians. Yaw is the spin around the vertical axis.

questions.correct: Sets the current heading to zero without moving the robot
wrong: Physically spins the robot back to face forward
Turns the IMU sensor completely off for now
Recharges the Control Hub's battery a little
questions.explain: resetYaw() re-zeros the heading reference wherever the robot is now — it does NOT move the robot, it just makes "here" count as 0.

questions.correct: It wakes the sensor and sets its mounting orientation
wrong: It spins the robot around to find true north
It charges the IMU right from the battery
It deletes any old heading readings first
questions.explain: initialize() wakes the IMU and tells it how the Control Hub is mounted (which way is up and forward), so its readings come out correct.

questions.q: What does the mounting orientation tell the IMU?
questions.correct: Which way the hub's logo and USB port face
wrong: How fast the robot is allowed to drive
Which motor ports the four wheels use
How many game pieces the robot can hold
questions.explain: You describe the hub's mounting with LogoFacingDirection and UsbFacingDirection (e.g., UP and FORWARD). Wrong values give scrambled heading readings on a real robot.

questions.correct: Converts radians into degrees for readable telemetry
wrong: Converts degrees into radians for the math
Rounds the heading down to a whole number
Resets the heading value back to zero
questions.explain: The code works in radians, but degrees are easier for humans to read. Math.toDegrees(heading) converts for display on the Driver Hub.

questions.q: The heading value ranges roughly from...
wrong: 0 to 100 percent
0 to 28 ticks
questions.explain: Heading runs about −π to +π (roughly −3.14 to +3.14 radians). Zero is straight ahead; the sign shows which way it turned.

questions.q: Why bind heading reset to a button like the right bumper?
questions.correct: So the driver can set "forward" to the current facing
wrong: So the robot drives noticeably faster after it
So the intake motor spins in reverse for a bit
So the telemetry shows a few more decimals
questions.explain: Pressing the bumper calls resetYaw(), making wherever the robot faces now count as forward (0). Handy for field-centric driving at match start.

questions.q: What kind of sensor is the IMU?
questions.correct: A gyroscope and accelerometer inside the Control Hub
wrong: A camera mounted on the front of the robot
A distance sensor aimed at the field wall
An encoder built into each drive motor
questions.explain: The IMU (inertial measurement unit) lives inside the Control Hub and combines a gyroscope and accelerometer. Its heading output is what you use most.

questions.q: If the IMU readings look inverted or scrambled, check...
questions.correct: The mounting orientation you gave in initialize()
wrong: The battery's remaining charge percentage
The name you gave your code package
The number of telemetry lines you print
questions.explain: Wrong LogoFacing/UsbFacing values mean the IMU misreads which way is up or forward, so headings come out flipped or scrambled. Fix the mounting description.

questions.q: A heading of 0 means the robot is...
wrong: Turned all the way around
Sitting with a dead battery
Moving at full speed forward
questions.explain: Heading starts at 0 in the direction the robot began (or wherever you last reset). Turning changes it up or down from there.

questions.correct: No, it only re-zeros the heading value
wrong: Yes, it spins the robot to face north
Yes, it drives the robot forward a bit
No, but it stops all the motors first
questions.explain: resetYaw() changes only the heading reference — the robot doesn't move. It just decides that the current facing now counts as 0.

questions.q: Why does the IMU report heading in radians, not degrees?
questions.correct: Because Math.cos and Math.sin both expect radians
wrong: Because degrees are against the FTC rules
Because radians make the robot drive faster
Because the battery only supports radians
questions.explain: The rotation math (cos and sin) works in radians, so the raw heading is in radians. You convert to degrees only when showing it to a human.
